_README: Which repair is approved for which survey. Keyed by survey unit —
'<Clan> — <Zone>', the same key the polygon layer uses.
A repair is approved for one survey at a time, by the person reviewing
that survey's map, and it applies to that survey and no other. A fix that
is right on one clan's data has been wrong on the next often enough that
this is the rule, not a precaution. Nothing here is a default, and
nothing is applied dataset-wide without being added, survey by survey,
after someone has looked at the map it changes.
collapse_duplicates — read the survey's open ends from one copy of each
stretch. The recording app saved many walks several times over under
names differing by a keystroke; each copy adds two endpoints, so a
real open end where copies stop reads as a junction, and a copy that
stopped short of the line it was copying leaves a phantom open end.
Topology only — walked distance, enclosure geometry and the stored
data all still come from every recording. See closure.distinct_indices.

why: 77 recorded parts carrying 9.4 km of distinct line. None of the twenty
open ends the pipeline could see was either of the two Max Mamo named.
Chord 1 was drawn from a phantom: the 169 m 'Raian water' recording
lies 0.0 m on top of the first 168 m of the 332 m 'Karira' track and
stops 2.7 m from a line that carries straight on.
With one copy of each stretch the two named ends come out unprompted,
first and fourth of eight, and the chord runs between them.
